serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Zeta Marketing Platform for Government (ZMP-GOV) is a
multi-tenant SaaS marketing platform for federal agencies.
The certified offering covers outbound email: audience
segmentation, campaign authoring, scheduling, delivery,
suppression management, and engagement reporting.
Agencies load their own contact lists and content. ZMP-GOV
sends the email and reports on delivery and engagement.
The service is hosted in AWS US East/West.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: FedRAMP Trust Center for the Cloud Service Offering.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions:
Not applicable. The FedRAMP trust center is public and
needs no login.
Access-controlled documents (the SOC 2 Type II report and
audit engagement documentation) are requested at
https://trust.zetaglobal.com using "Get access". Requests
from .gov and .mil addresses are reviewed by Zeta's security
team.
trustCenter.agencyAccessDenialProcess:
1. Agencies request FedRAMP Certification Data through
the trust center at https://trust.paramify.com/zetaglobal/zeta-
global. Public certification data (this overview, the service
list, the External Framework Mapping, and Ongoing
Certification Reports) is available without a request.
2. Access-controlled materials are released to requesters
with a verified .gov or .mil email address, or to agency-
designated contractors on written confirmation from the
agency, on acceptance of Zeta's terms of use.
3. Zeta expects to grant all agency requests. If Zeta denies a
request (for example, the requester cannot be verified as
acting for an agency), Zeta records the reason, tells the
requester, and notifies FedRAMP through the CSP Agency
Access Denial form at help.fedramp.gov within 5 business
days of the denial (CDS-UTC-AAD).
4. Denials and the FedRAMP notification are logged by the
Security contact and summarized in the next Ongoing
Certification Report.

informationResources.summary:
ZMP-GOV is the set of information resources that handle
federal customer data (agency contact lists, message
content, and the delivery and engagement records tied to
those contacts) or that can affect its confidentiality, integrity,
or availability (MAS-CSO-IIR).
The set is: (1) the ZMP-GOV application services that run
the email channel; (2) the data stores behind them; (3) the
ID lookup service that converts customer identifiers to ZID
tokens; (4) the email delivery infrastructure; (5) the build,
logging, and monitoring systems that operate the platform;
and (6) the Zeta personnel, policies, and procedures that run
it. All machine-based resources are hosted in AWS US
East/West.
Third-party information resources are listed in Section 8.
Federal customer data leaves the certified set only as ZID-
tokenized engagement records sent to the reporting
warehouse (Section 8, Non-Certified Resource 2).
informationResources.explicitExclusions:
1. Zeta Data Cloud and the Identity Supergraph. ZMP-GOV
reaches Data Cloud only through ZID tokens produced by
the in-scope ID lookup service. Raw federal customer
identifiers are not sent to Data Cloud.
2. ZMP channels other than email (SMS, push, web, and
programmatic advertising) and other Zeta products (Cheetah
Digital and Loyalty, Sailthru, LiveClicker, Selligent).
3. Zeta on-premise (VMware) infrastructure. None of it
serves ZMP-GOV.
4. Zeta corporate business systems, including the
Salesforce sales CRM. Contact data about agency staff held
for sales purposes is not federal customer data placed in
ZMP-GOV.
5. Agency-side resources: agency workstations, browsers,
identity providers, and the mail systems that receive ZMP-
GOV email.
6. No software is delivered for installation on agency
systems (see fedramp.gov/scope). The offering is used
through the ZMP-GOV web application and APIs.

resources.name: ZMP-GOV application services
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Containerized microservices on Amazon EKS that provide
the email channel: web application and APIs, audience
segmentation, campaign authoring and template
management, scheduling, send orchestration, suppression
and preference management, bounce and complaint
handling, and engagement reporting. Multi-tenant; federal
tenants are logically separated by tenant identifier.

resources.name: ZMP-GOV data stores
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Operational data stores for the application services:
Aerospike and ScyllaDB (profile and campaign state),
Amazon Aurora (relational configuration and metadata),
Kafka with ZooKeeper (event streaming), Elasticsearch
(search and reporting indexes), Amazon EMR (batch
processing), and Amazon S3 (object storage for lists,
content assets, and exports). Encrypted at rest with AWS
KMS keys.

resources.name: ID lookup service (Maui / IDaaS)
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Converts agency-supplied customer identifiers (such as
email addresses) into Zeta ID (ZID) tokens. Runs inside the
certified set. ZIDs let ZMP-GOV exchange data with
systems outside the certified set (the reporting warehouse
and Zeta Data Cloud) without sending raw federal customer
identifiers. This is the tokenization boundary for the offering.

resources.name: Email delivery infrastructure
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Mail transfer agents and sending IP pools that deliver
campaign email to recipient mail systems, receive bounces
and feedback-loop complaints, and record delivery events.
Outbound mail uses TLS to recipient servers that support it.
DKIM signing and SPF and DMARC alignment are
configured per sending domain.

resources.name: Build and deployment tooling
resources.descriptionAndRole:
GitLab source control and CI/CD pipelines, container
registry, infrastructure-as-code, secrets management, and
feature configuration used to build and deploy ZMP-GOV.
These systems hold no federal customer data but control
what code and configuration run in production.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Integrity and availability. A compromised pipeline could
deploy unauthorized code or configuration. Changes are
logged (KSI-CMT-LMC), peer-reviewed, and reach
production only through the pipeline.

resources.name: Logging, monitoring, and vulnerability detection
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Centralized application and infrastructure logs (AWS
CloudTrail, CloudWatch, and the platform log store), metrics
and alerting, and vulnerability scanning of hosts, containers,
and dependencies (AWS Inspector and CIS Level 1
benchmark checks). Logs may contain metadata about
federal customer data (tenant, campaign, and message
identifiers, and event timestamps) and are in scope under
MAS-CSO-MDI.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Confidentiality (log metadata), integrity, and availability
(detection and audit evidence).

resources.name: Zeta operations, security, and support personnel
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Zeta engineering, site reliability, security operations, and
customer support staff with administrative access to ZMP-
GOV, and the policies and procedures they follow: access
control, change management, incident response,
vulnerability management, and security training. Access is
granted by role through Okta with phishing-resistant
passwordless authentication, reviewed quarterly, and
removed automatically on termination. Privileged sessions
are logged.

alternativeSecurityFramework.impactLevelScope:
SOC 2 Type II for the Zeta Marketing Platform (ZMP): the
production environment, its supporting AWS infrastructure,
and the engineering, security, and operations processes that
run it.
Trust Services Criteria in scope: Security, Availability, and
Confidentiality.
alternativeSecurityFramework.mappingToFedRampRules:
Zeta maps the SOC 2 Type II report to the 23 mandatory
Class A rules (FRC-CLA-MFR) in the External Framework
Mapping on the trust center
(https://trust.paramify.com/zetaglobal/zeta-
global/controls/73974d0d-ddfc-4992-b32d-2699e0f4ec8d).
Summary:
1. Identity and access (KSI-IAM-AAM, KSI-IAM-APM). SOC
2 CC6.1 to CC6.3 cover provisioning, deprovisioning, and
access reviews. Automated account lifecycle and phishing-
resistant passwordless authentication for privileged users
are implemented through Okta and evidenced separately,
since SOC 2 does not require passwordless.
2. Network restriction (KSI-CNA-RNT). CC6.6 and CC6.7
cover boundary protection and transmission security.
Evidence: VPC security groups, deny-by-default network
policies, TLS 1.2 or higher.
3. Change logging (KSI-CMT-LMC). CC8.1 covers change
management. Evidence: pipeline and infrastructure change
logs tied to reviewed changes.
4. Training review (KSI-CED-RAT). CC1.4 and CC2.2 cover
security awareness training. Annual review of training
content is tracked separately.
5. Incident response (KSI-INR-RIR, IEC-CSO-EFR, IEC-
CSO-FIR). CC7.3 to CC7.5 cover incident detection,
response, and recovery. FedRAMP reportability evaluation,
PAIN rating, and the 3-business-day Final Incident Report
are FedRAMP-specific additions to the incident response
plan.
6. Securing information (KSI-SVC-SIN). CC6.1, CC6.7, and
C1.1 cover encryption at rest and in transit and
confidentiality of customer data.
7. Vulnerability detection (VDR-CSO-DET). CC7.1 and
CC7.2 cover vulnerability scanning and monitoring.
Evidence: AWS Inspector, dependency and container
scanning, annual penetration testing, and the Bugcrowd
vulnerability disclosure program.
8. Scope and third parties (MAS-CSO-IIR). CC9.2 covers
vendor risk management. The resource inventory in
Sections 6 and 8 is FedRAMP-specific.
9. Rules with no SOC 2 counterpart, implemented as new
FedRAMP processes: FRC-CSO-PKG, FRC-CSO-JSN,
FRC-CSO-POP, CDS-CSO-PUB, CDS-CSO-UTC, CDS-
UTC-AAD, AFC-CSO-INB, AFC-CSO-RCV, AFC-CSO-CRA,
CCM-OCR-AVL, CCM-OCR-NRD. These are met through
the Paramify trust center, the FedRAMP Security Inbox, and
the quarterly Ongoing Certification Report.
10. Annual assessment (IVV-CSX-AIA). The annual SOC 2
Type II audit is the persistent independent assessment for
Class A.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription:
Outbound email campaign management for federal
agencies. Includes audience segmentation, campaign
authoring, template management, scheduling, delivery,
suppression and preference management, bounce and
complaint handling, and engagement reporting.

thirdPartyInformationResources.metadataIncludedInScope:
Yes. Metadata about federal customer data is included in
the Minimum Assessment Scope (MAS-CSO-MDI):
1. Campaign and message metadata: campaign and
template identifiers, send schedules and timestamps,
sending domain.
2. Delivery and engagement events keyed to recipient
identifiers: sent, delivered, bounced, opened, clicked,
unsubscribed, complained.
3. Suppression and preference list entries, audience
segment definitions, and segment counts.
4. Tenant configuration, user accounts, and audit and
access logs that reference federal customer records.
Engagement metadata exported to the reporting warehouse
is keyed by ZID token, not by raw recipient identifier.

certified.fedRampCertifiedThirdPartyInformationRes:
AGENCYAMAZONEW (AWS US East/West, FedRAMP
Certified Class C (Moderate), Rev5, JAB path)
certified.useCase:
Sole IaaS provider for the ZMP-GOV certified set. No on-
premise or alternate cloud infrastructure is used.
certified.usageAndConfiguration:
Compute (Amazon EKS and EC2), object and block storage
(S3 and EBS), managed databases (Aurora), batch
processing (EMR), networking (VPC, load balancers), key
management (KMS), and logging (CloudTrail and
CloudWatch).
Deployed in AWS US East/West commercial regions within
Zeta's AWS Organization. Federal tenants run in the same
account structure as Zeta commercial production, with
logical separation by tenant identifier.
certified.justificationForUse:
Required to operate the offering. AWS US East/West holds
FedRAMP Certified Class C (Moderate), so the physical,
environmental, and hypervisor controls inherited from AWS
are covered by that certification. The AWS services used for
ZMP-GOV are within the AWS US East/West FedRAMP
scope.
certified.mitigationMeasures:
FIPS-validated service endpoints. Encryption at rest with
customer-managed KMS keys and in transit with TLS 1.2 or
higher. CIS Level 1 hardening on instances and container
images. Deny-by-default security groups and Kubernetes
network policies.
certified.compensatingControls:
Administrative access to AWS is through Okta SSO with
phishing-resistant passwordless authentication and role-
based IAM. Privileged sessions use AWS Systems Manager
Session Manager with session logging. CloudTrail and
CloudWatch logs are retained centrally and reviewed. AWS
Inspector scans hosts and images. Tenant data is separated
at the application and data-store layers.

certified.useCase:
Compliance documentation platform and FedRAMP-
compatible trust center.
certified.usageAndConfiguration:
SaaS. Holds the Certification Package Overview, the
Security Decision Record, the External Framework Mapping,
and evidence metadata; produces the machine-readable
(JSON) package; hosts the trust center at
https://trust.paramify.com/zetaglobal/zeta-global. Zeta
compliance staff sign in through SSO with MFA.
certified.justificationForUse:
Required to produce and publish certification data in human-
readable and JSON formats (FRC-CSO-PKG, FRC-CSO-
JSN) and to meet the trust center rule (CDS-CSO-UTC).
certified.mitigationMeasures:
No federal customer data is sent to Paramify. Content is
limited to security documentation, control narratives, and
evidence metadata.
certified.compensatingControls:
Zeta keeps responsibility for the accuracy of all published
information (FRC-CSO-MRA). Publication requires review by
the Security contact. Evidence integrations use least-
privilege, read-only credentials.

nonCertified.name: Okta IDaaS
nonCertified.useCase:
Workforce identity for privileged and administrative access
to the certified set.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration:
SSO, MFA, and phishing-resistant passwordless
authentication for Zeta staff accessing AWS, Kubernetes,
and ZMP-GOV administrative interfaces. Device posture and
session policies are applied.
nonCertified.justificationForUse:
Satisfies KSI-IAM-APM (passwordless), which is mandatory
at Class A. No alternate identity provider is in the certified
set.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures:
Passwordless enrollment is required for all privileged roles.
Okta holds Zeta workforce identities only; no federal
customer data. Quarterly access reviews.
nonCertified.compensatingControls:
Account creation and removal are automated (KSI-IAM-
AAM), so departed staff lose access on termination.
Authentication and administrative events are sent to Zeta's
central log store and reviewed.

nonCertified.name: Snowflake (commercial regions)
nonCertified.useCase:
Cloud data warehouse for campaign performance and
engagement analytics supporting the certified Email
Marketing service.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration:
Deployed in Snowflake commercial regions on AWS. Access
restricted to named service accounts through SSO with
MFA. No public endpoint. Data flow is one-directional:
Snowflake is a reporting sink and does not write back into
campaign targeting or suppression logic.
nonCertified.justificationForUse:
Snowflake is the reporting warehouse for ZMP. Engagement
reporting for federal tenants uses the same warehouse.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures:
Engagement records are keyed by ZID token; raw recipient
identifiers (such as email addresses) do not leave the
certified set. Federal tenant rows are separated by tenant
identifier under row access policies. Transport uses TLS 1.2
or higher.
nonCertified.compensatingControls:
Warehouse access is logged and reviewed. Service account
credentials are held in secrets management. Snowflake's
SOC 2 Type II report is reviewed under Zeta's vendor risk
process.
